input.quote: Each Service Option Attachment will renew automatically for an additional term equal in duration to the previous term of the applicable Service Option Attachment unless either party notifies the other party in writing at least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the then-current term for the applicable Service Option Attachment that it has elected to terminate such Service Option Attachment.
input.rationale: § 3.2 provides automatic renewal but requires ninety (90) days' written notice to avoid it, which exceeds our fallback ceiling of a 60-day non-renewal notice window (and is 60 days beyond our preferred 30-day opt-out). We have therefore taken the shortest cure and shortened the window to sixty (60) days, landing the clause at the fallback. No provision anywhere in the Agreement permits a renewal price increase — Charges are fixed by the Service Option Attachments and Order Forms (§ 4.1) — so the conditional uplift element is already satisfied. We note but do not redline that renewal terms track the duration of the previous term rather than being capped at 12 months, and that there is no Vendor renewal reminder; those are preferred-only points, though we would resist any multi-year Order Form term given the roll-forward effect.

mappings.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
mappings.quote: Charges for applicable Services will be specified in Service Option Attachments and Order Forms.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have shortened the non-renewal notice window in § 3.2 from ninety to sixty days so we can exit an automatic renewal within our fallback 60-day window; our preferred position is a 30-day opt-out with a renewal reminder.
proposal.summary: Shorten non-renewal notice window from 90 to 60 days in § 3.2.
